subject: Post-demo: 1M-token sanity check + next competitive tests
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-29T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: 1M-token sanity check + next competitive tests

Jordan — thanks again for hopping on the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the competitive economics work: 

Summary from the demo
- You saw a live comparison of response latency and a short unit-cost sketch. Acme wants a focused, repeatable way to compare per-1M-token economics across providers for your generative search workload (8k context average, mixed chat + completion).
- Key asks from your side: direct per-1M-token delta vs HyperscalerX, an A/B run with and without prefix/KV cache, and a realistic batching profile (p95 latency target ~200ms).

What we propose
1) Sanity test (1M tokens): run a 1M-token synthetic workload that mirrors your mix (70% short chat, 30% long completion, 8k avg context) to surface raw unit cost numbers. Deliverable: per-1M-token cost at p50/p95 with and without KV cache. (attachment: redwood_acme_1m-token-modeling.xlsx)
2) Cache sensitivity: two runs with KV cache hit targets: 30% (baseline) and 70% (optimized) to show cost slope with cache. We'll provide test harness and metrics to validate hit rates. (attachment: kv-cache-test-specs.md)
3) Batching matrix: small/medium/large batch sizes (continuous batching) to show latency vs cost tradeoffs and practical batch sizes that meet your p95 SLA.
4) HyperscalerX parity run: we will provide test scripts you can run against HyperscalerX and we can run against Redwood (hosted + dedicated) so apples-to-apples comparison (same model variant and tokenization).

Initial Redwood delta estimates (very rough):
- Redwood hosted (optimized batching + 50% cache hit): ~$11.5 per 1M tokens
- Redwood dedicated (reserved capacity + quantized model): ~$7.2 per 1M tokens (after committed capacity)
- HyperscalerX public endpoint (no cache, default batch): ~$17.8 per 1M tokens

These are estimates to set expectations — the 1M-run will surface the real numbers.

Next steps / asks for you
- Please confirm whether Acme can run the HyperscalerX-side scripts (we'll provide instructions) or if you prefer Redwood to run both sides in a test account.
- Approve the test window: proposed 9/6–9/8 (3 days) to run both cache scenarios + batching matrix.
- If procurement wants to join the thread, add them and we'll include a short SOW for the testing engagement.

I attached the modeling sheet and test spec. Ben & Laura — looping you for pricing / ops input and to coordinate the test infra.

Cheers,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_acme_1m-token-modeling.xlsx (xlsx))
(attachment: kv-cache-test-specs.md (text))

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T08:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: 1M-token sanity check + next competitive tests

Thanks, Soojin — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) HyperscalerX: procurement flagged that they won't run third-party scripts in our prod environment. We can provision a test project in our sandbox where Redwood can run both sides, or Redwood can provide exact curl/python scripts we run internally. Sandbox access preferred.
2) Dataset: we'll provide a 100k token seed corpus (anonymized queries + responses) you can reuse for the synthetic run to make results comparable. ETA for that data: 9/3.
3) Cost priorities: our initial gating metric is per-1M-token delta at our expected cache hit (we estimate 35% initially). Secondary is tail latency (p95) at scale.

Procurement - looping you for SOW sign-off on a short paid engagement (~2 engineer-days of Redwood test support + infra credit).

Jordan
Jordan Mills
Senior Product Manager, Search
Acme Cloud Services

On Aug 29, 2027, at 3:02 PM, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks again for hopping on the call earlier...

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-31T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo: 1M-token sanity check + next competitive tests (pricing + ops notes)

Soojin — notes from pricing/ops side and a suggested runbook: 

Pricing assumptions we should validate before the run
- Token definition: use the same tokenizer and model variant for all providers (we recommend the open-variant matching the demo weights).
- Effective infra mix: for Redwood hosted numbers above I assumed mixed A100-style instances with our continuous batching; dedicated assumes committed A10x2-ish profile and 70% utilization. We'll capture instance-level cost breakdown in the sheet.

Suggested minimum test matrix (we can run subsets if Acme prefers):
A) Baseline: 1M tokens, no cache, default batch -> measure cost / p50 / p95.
B) Cache sensitivity: repeat A with 30% and 70% KV hit targets (we'll instrument and report hit-rate).
C) Batching sweep: target p95 <= 200ms, test batch sizes {4,8,16,32} to show cost/latency curve.
D) Dedicated vs Hosted: run the baseline on a dedicated nodepool (if Acme approves reserved nodes) to demonstrate committed-unit economics.

Operational asks
- We need sandbox credentials by 9/4 to start infra prep.
- Engineering will need 1 engineer (Redwood) + 1 Acme engineer the test days to validate runs.
- I'll prep the redwood_acme_1m-token-modeling.xlsx with an explicit per-component line item (gpu-hours, storage, infra markup).

Preliminary unit numbers (for internal planning only):
- Redwood hosted (with continuous batching + ~50% effective cache): $11.50 / 1M tokens
- Redwood dedicated (post-commit): $7.20 / 1M tokens
- HyperscalerX public endpoint (as-published / default): $17.80 / 1M tokens
- Note: if KV cache hit improves to 70% Redwood hosted can drop to ~$7.8 / 1M tokens in some workloads.

I'll attach the updated sheet after I populate the infra line items. Priyom — can you confirm we have a dedicated test nodepool available 9/6–9/8 if Acme wants that?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_acme_1m-token-modeling.xlsx (xlsx))

Thanks everyone — quick alignment and proposed timeline: 

1) Data & sandbox: Jordan will provide seed corpus by 9/3 and procurement will confirm sandbox access by 9/4. We will not run anything in Acme prod.
2) Infra prep (Redwood): Ben/Priyom to provision a temporary dedicated nodepool (if Acme approves) and a hosted experiment project by 9/5.
3) Test window: 9/6–9/8 as proposed. Deliverables: raw logs, per-1M-token cost table (p50/p95), hit-rate graphs, and an exec summary comparing Redwood hosted/dedicated vs HyperscalerX.
4) Responsibilities: 
- Redwood: test harness, run hosted side, assist with HyperscalerX scripts if needed.
- Acme: provide sandbox credentials & seed corpus, run HyperscalerX scripts (or grant Redwood sandbox run permission).

Action items: 
- Jordan: share dataset and confirm sandbox permissions (deadline 9/4).
- Procurement: confirm budget for the short SOW (Ben will send cost estimate).
- Ben/Priyom: publish the final modeling sheet and test harness repo by 9/5.

If that works, I'll open a short SOW draft and a calendar invite for the test run days.

Thanks — excited to get apples-to-apples data for you.

—Soojin
